parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile federal layer with a mixed state layer. Visitor-facing exposures are documented: a February 2025 consular cable directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; federally funded single-sex facilities are barred to trans people nationwide, including here; immigration and federal custody show documented abuse (beatings, solitary, sexual abuse, forced hormone/hair removal). A trans minor cannot obtain transition care here. Offsetting: this state criminalises no gender expression, its facility bill failed, restroom use is unrestricted (two cities protect it), hate-crime statutes cover gender identity, and courts have enjoined several federal orders. Public opinion (66–69% backing birth-sex rules) signals real social hostility.

entry_documents.exposure: Documented: Feb 2025 cable tells officers to refuse where documents/records cast reasonable doubt on sex, and to weigh fraud-based lifetime ineligibility; X markers barred for new issues; body-scanner/pat-down outing risk; eight-plus governments issued travel advisories about trans visitors.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, has limited waivers and is never automatic; challenges pending in national courts; legal-aid FAQ tracks document rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal or document doubt can cascade into immigration detention, where abuse of trans detainees is documented; a discrepancy at one crossing can travel with the visitor for the whole trip.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: trans men in immigration custody reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; from 2026 federal corrections adopted conversion-therapy-style policy (hair cutting, hormone removal, psychiatric drugs) for transgender inmates; reporting of trans prisoner numbers stopped in 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Federal and state hate-crime statutes cover gender identity; courts are functioning and have blocked several orders; the birth-sex prison-housing bill in this state never passed the lower chamber.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy → investigation/fraud allegation → federal detention → conversion-style custody policy; the state layer does not shield anyone from federal custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Documented nationally: executive order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities; across units 9+1 ban congruent use in all government buildings, 9 more partly, 3 schools-only, and 4 units make it a criminal offence in certain circumstances (one arrest recorded, 2025, held 24 hours in the men's ward).
federal_state_facilities.protection: Documented locally: as of April 2026 this state places no restriction on restroom use matching gender identity, two cities affirmatively protect it, and criminalisation bills died in committee since 2021.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The same visitor loses access inside federal buildings while state and municipal spaces here remain open; travel to other units instantly changes the exposure to bans or trespass charges.

care_services.exposure: Documented: this state bars transition procedures, puberty blockers and hormones for anyone under 18 (upheld Nov 2024), so a trans minor visitor cannot obtain care; national proposals would deny insurance reimbursement to trans under-18s; the LGBTQ youth crisis-lifeline service was shut in 2025.
care_services.protection: Not documented for adult visitors — sources are silent on adult care availability here.
care_services.interaction: A travelling family with a trans minor faces care denial that is criminal for the provider, pushing any need toward emergency care, where facility and record-exposure rules then apply.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented: executive orders call gender-affirming care 'mutilation' and direct law enforcement to investigate 'gender ideology' in schools; a May 2026 counterterrorism strategy targets groups 'radically pro-transgender'; 2025 polls show 66% backing birth-sex markers and 69% the sports ban; 190+ anti-LGBTQ bills introduced in 2023.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The same memo says rewards are not tied to gender ideology and that counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; national employment and hate-crime protections remain in force.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises the probability of outing and of bystander or officer hostility, while functioning courts and statutes give the outed traveller somewhere to turn.

minors_guardians.exposure: Documented: transition care for under-18s banned here (criminal liability for physicians); a trans minor is barred from congruent federally funded facilities; the federal directive framing social transition as exploitative raises risk if a school-age child is identified.
minors_guardians.protection: Parent-specific prosecution or custody exposure for visiting families is not documented; several federal orders are enjoined; hate-crime statutes apply to minors as victims.
minors_guardians.interaction: Care denial plus facility exclusion means a travelling trans minor is most exposed precisely in routine settings (clinic, federal building), not only at the border.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented at low level: a national travel guide advises checking recent violence reports; polling shows a social majority favouring birth-sex documentation; no patterned trans-specific killing or organised targeting is recorded anywhere in the dossier.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime law (2019) adds gender identity as an aggravating circumstance, backed by the federal hate-crime statute; same-sex conduct decriminalised since 1977; no state sodomy law; two cities protect facility use.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Public disapproval mostly produces friction, but where it escalates the enhanced-sentence and federal hate-crime machinery gives a working, if untested, remedy.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unresolved: the civil-liberties challenge to the licence-marker ban and passport suits are pending; no enforcement data on gender-identity hate-crime charges; whether the religious-freedom statute covers gender identity is inconsistently sourced; risk assessments call this unit among the harshest in the country.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have blocked or enjoined multiple federal orders, an appellate injunction protects students' facility use, an ACLU suit and a running legal-aid FAQ operate, and 22 units plus the capital outlaw gender-identity discrimination.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are real but slow and geography-dependent: which federal measure is in force on the travel date materially changes exposure, and outcomes vary unit to unit.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.35-A: Vellandra runs a universal Visitor Conduct Register barring all transgender entrants with no remedy. Here refusal is conditional on document discrepancy, is never automatic on the fraud ground, and pending litigation plus functioning courts offer a real, if slow, challenge.

Lower than 0.55-B: Kestrel Isles offers only variable secondary screening and administrative refusal. Here an outed traveller also faces federal facility exclusion, a minor-care ban, and immigration/federal custody with documented beatings, solitary and sexual abuse — materially worse than screening friction alone.

Lower than 0.75-C: Meridia has trained border officers, a tribunal awarding compensation and no special questioning. Here the consular cable actively directs refusal on sex doubt, foreign states warn their citizens away, and custody abuse is documented — a documented exposure, not an open question.

Similar in kind to 0.45-D: Drellia's nightly database transmission produces durable exposure with slow, opaque remedies. Comparable — routine, unavoidable disclosure risk plus weak redress — but aggravated here by custody abuse and a possible lifetime entry bar, pushing slightly below it.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one system: a federal layer that withholds markers, instructs refusal on sex doubt, excludes trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities, and detains abusively, overlaid on a state layer that is comparatively permissive on facilities and expression but bans minor transition care. Universal exposures (facility exclusion, entry screening, social majority hostility) sit alongside low-probability, high-severity ones (immigration detention abuse, federal conversion-style custody). Protections are genuine — hate-crime statutes, injunctions, pending suits, no local criminalisation — but they operate after harm and are uneven across units. Net: credible everyday friction plus conditional severe escalation, with remedies that work slowly; not a systematic exclusion regime, clearly worse than routine-screening jurisdictions.
